cases.name: keepalive lifecycle: role welcome, heartbeats, tool call/answer, clean end
cases.vector: stub agent role=architect keepalive: hello -> welcome(role,keepalive) -> 12 heartbeats (the hub's rate-limited line) -> guest tool_call -> hub tool_result -> bye -> the row drains

invariants.name: welcome echoes the accepted role and the keepalive flag
the hub logged the connect transition with the role
the hub logged exactly the rate-limited heartbeat lines (1st and 12th)
the hub answered the guest's echo tool call
the hub logged the answered guest call
the hub answered the guest's uptime tool call
the registry row carries the cid, the accepted role and the call count
last_heartbeat advanced across the beats
the hub logged a clean end after 2 tool calls
the hub closed the session after the bye
the registry row drained after the bye

notes: direction covered: the guest-initiated tool_call -> hub tool_result (and the guest's bye). The hub-initiated tool_call/stop direction has no producer in this build (the session's steering sender, Hub::steer, is #[cfg(test)]; nothing in the daemon fills it this slice), so it is exercised by the crate's own UDS test and is not drivable from an acceptance stub.

cases.name: reconnect across a hub restart: clean rebind over stale listeners, re-registration, v1 unaffected
cases.vector: stub keepalive builder -> SIGKILL vsockd (its listener files are left behind) -> restart on the SAME uds dir and CIDs -> re-hello registers afresh -> one v1 session after the restart

invariants.name: the first session is a keepalive builder session
the daemon died ungracefully (SIGKILL)
the ungraceful death left a stale listener file behind (the path a restart must clear)
the agent's connection dropped with the daemon
the restarted hub rebound over the stale listener files
the agent reconnects and is welcomed again
the restarted hub logged the agent's registration
the registry shows the agent again with a fresh connected_at
the re-registered session serves a tool call
the re-registered session ends cleanly
a v1 session after the restart gets the frozen welcome byte-shape
the v1 session's tool calls are answered end to end
the v1 session ends cleanly and the hub logs it

notes: the contract's `re-adopted` line fires when a reconnect replaces a LIVE row; a restarted hub has an empty in-memory registry, so a post-restart reconnect registers afresh (asserted here). Live-row replacement is proven deterministically by the re-adoption case.

cases.name: re-adoption: a same-CID reconnect replaces a live row (the contract's re-adopted line)
cases.vector: two concurrent sessions on one CID: the second re-adopts the live row (logged), and the predecessor's disconnect cannot evict its successor's row

invariants.name: both sessions are welcomed as keepalive builders
the hub logged the re-adoption of the live row
the adopted session is still served after the predecessor leaves
the registry still carries the adopted row (the predecessor could not evict it)
the adopted session ends cleanly

cases.name: reap/hangup contract: no premature reap, a silent agent stays alive, every row drains
cases.vector: keepalive reviewer silent 10s (the deadline is 300s) then still served; a disconnect without bye drains the row; 3 further connect/drop cycles leave 0 rows

invariants.name: the agent is welcomed as a keepalive reviewer
no premature reap inside the observation window
the registry row persists across the silence
the silent agent is still served (it was not reaped)
the hub reported the dropped connection as a loss, not a protocol violation
the dropped session's row drained
every churn connection was accepted
3 connect/drop cycles leave the registry at 0 (no row leak)
no reap was ever logged (nothing went silent past the deadline)

notes: the 300s reap deadline itself is unit-tested in the crate with an injected clock (a real 300 s wait has no place in an acceptance run); this case asserts the observable half — no reap inside a bounded silence, and a drained registry on every disconnect path.

cases.name: a reused work directory is refused (a regression case)
cases.vector: deterministic fixtures, no daemon: a fresh (or empty, or absent) directory is accepted, while a directory holding an earlier run's daemon log (whose `listening on` line would satisfy the readiness wait against a dead port) or an earlier run's per-CID socket file is refused with the reason

invariants.name: a work directory that does not exist yet is accepted (the runner makes one)
an empty work directory is accepted (an operator may pre-create one)
a directory holding an earlier run's daemon log is refused, naming the readiness hazard
invariants.detail: reason="it already holds leftovers from an earlier run: the daemon logs 'demo-logs' (a stale `listening on` line satisfies a readiness wait and the harness then talks to a dead port) — a reused directory silently defeats the harness's readiness waits, so this run's results would mix two runs' state"

invariants.name: a directory holding an earlier run's socket file is refused too (existence is not a listener)
invariants.detail: reason="it already holds leftovers from an earlier run: the socket directory 'demo-uds' (a stale socket path is not a live listener) — a reused directory silently defeats the harness's readiness waits, so this run's results would mix two runs' state"

invariants.name: any other leftover still refuses the directory (only a directory the runner can call its own is used)
invariants.detail: reason="it already holds leftovers from an earlier run: entries starting 'notes.txt' — a reused directory silently defeats the harness's readiness waits, so this run's results would mix two runs' state"

notes: the refusal is at the runner's door (Ctx): run.py reports it as BLOCKED (exit 2) with the reason, so a reused directory can never silently mix two runs' artifacts into one result row.
